- If sentiment is high (≥0.6) in recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slightly.
- If model shows strong upward trend after a spike, it often overshoots; cap forecast at 1–2% above recent peak.
- When true outcome shows sharp drop after a spike, model often fails to correct; add downward bias in next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is low (≤0.2) and price is rising, model may overreact; reduce forecast slope.
- Model often underestimates true price when sentiment is volatile (alternating highs/lows); use sentiment median as adjustment factor.
- For 30-day horizon, if forecast is flat or rising slowly but true outcome shows strong volatility, reduce forecast by 1–3% to account for mean reversion.
- If sentiment history shows recent negative sentiment (e.g., 0.1–0.3) and price is rising, model may be overconfident; adjust downward by 0.5–1.5%.
- When true outcome is significantly lower than forecast (e.g., >5% gap), check if sentiment was high recently — if so, reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
